content.comment_body: Hello, I've recently encountered several of these [product_name] controllers which have managed 6 air conditioning units in a room for about 15 years. Now only 2 AC units remain, but the previous parameters for the removed units still exist in the controller, causing problems for the remaining units. I want to adjust the configuration using the controller itself if possible. The current setup involves one input/output channel per AC unit. If a unit faults, the corresponding input will disengage and the output will prevent the unit from operating. The controller can then try to activate another available unit or two. Units also rotate automatically every 7 days. Can anyone advise which parameters I should review and modify to reflect the removal of two AC units? I'm not planning a full software rewrite, just a minor update if possible. Thanks in advance.
Welcome to the forum. Could you upload your [product_name] program as a zip file?

Without the appropriate software and programming cable, it's challenging to assist with this limited information. You can download the demo software for free. If you don't have a cable, you'll need to manually input the program step by step as displayed on the controller. Be sure to select the correct [product_name] type, e.g. [article_no]. You could also share photos showing parts of the program and parameters on the controller display, as well as a photo of its type. That might help others support you. Regards, [user_name]
I don't have a programming cable but I'll be onsite today and aim to gather more details from the controller to share back here. I’ll follow up later.
I tried uploading four videos but they were too large, so I've added them at the following links for reference: [url], [url], [url], [url]. Hopefully these are helpful.
The third link ([url]) does not seem to contain a video.

Personally, the videos aren't very helpful, and the same issue may apply to photo collections. The [product_name] controller uses a graphical interface similar to a spreadsheet, but we only see individual cells instead of the full logic. There is a risk of unintentional changes if the wrong button is pressed. Start by downloading the operating instructions for your [product_name] and review the chapters on manual programming and reading the diagram. It's a lengthy process if you lack the software and cable. While reviewing the diagram, you can recreate a file in the demo software. Remember to check all adjustable parameters (like timer settings) via the SetParam menu. Editing via display is not something I recommend, as it's error-prone and tedious. Regards, [user_name]
Is it possible to view the entire program logic using just the controller, without software or cable? If so, how can I access all this information?
Here's a resource for downloading manuals for older [product_name] controllers: [document]

You can't view the whole program at once, only individual cells, and it's unclear how many rows or columns there are without further effort. You'll have to work through each cell manually. Try this after downloading the relevant controller instructions. Another issue without software and cable is that maintenance and further changes will be difficult. Upload a photo or provide the full [article_no] from your controller. If it's one of the very early [product_name] models like [article_no], replacing it may be worth considering. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The main challenge is that the user is trying to modify settings on a long-used [product_name] controller after removing some devices, but direct access and editing from the device is tedious and unreliable. Without the correct programming cable or software, users must manually transcribe and adjust logic cell by cell, which is both time-consuming and prone to mistakes. The community finds this approach inefficient and recommends using proper interfaces or considering replacement when working with older hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to easily view and change critical control parameters directly from the hardware interface, ideally without relying on specialized programming cables or external software. They are looking for a straightforward solution that minimizes risk of error and technical difficulty.
